info.name: Food Surplus API
info.description:
Food Surplus platform API — auth, food categories, and admin.

=== SETUP ===
1. Set `base_url` if the API is not on http://127.0.0.1:8000/api
2. Run any Register or Login request — the token is saved into the `token` variable automatically, so every other request just works.

=== RESPONSE SHAPE ===
Every response, success or error, looks like this:
{ "success": bool, "data": object|null, "message": string|null, "errors": object|null }

So you can write ONE response handler for the whole app:
- success == true  -> read `data`
- success == false -> show `message`, and on 422 show `errors` under each field

Status codes: 200 OK · 201 Created · 401 Unauthenticated · 403 Forbidden · 404 Not found · 422 Validation error · 429 Too many requests.

=== ENUMS (fixed values — never send anything else) ===

1) type — the donor's kind. Required by POST /register/donor
   "individual" -> a private person
   "restaurant" -> a restaurant
   "hotel"      -> a hotel
   "company"    -> a company

3) status — the charity's account state. READ-ONLY (the API sets it, you only display it)
   "pending"   -> just registered, waiting for the admin. Can log in, but every charity feature returns 403.
   "active"    -> approved by the admin. Full access.
   "suspended" -> blocked by the admin. Can log in to see this, but no access.
   => After login, if data.type == "charity", branch on data.user.status to pick the screen.

4) data.type — which kind of account just logged in (returned by register / login / me)
   "donor" | "charity"  -> use it to decide which home screen to open.

Booleans are real JSON booleans (true/false), not 0/1 or "true".
Times are "HH:MM:SS" (e.g. "08:00:00"). Dates are ISO 8601 UTC.


5) status (on a donation request) — READ-ONLY, the API drives it
   "pending"    -> published, waiting for a charity to accept
   "accepted"   -> a charity took it; charity + eta_minutes are now filled in
   "picked_up"  -> the donor confirmed the handover; the food changed hands
   "completed"  -> the charity filed its distribution numbers
   "cancelled"  -> the donor cancelled (see cancel_reason)
   "expired"    -> valid_until passed with nobody taking it
   "no_show"    -> the charity accepted but never came (phase 3)
   CAREFUL: "pending" here means "waiting for a charity". The charity ACCOUNT
   status (item 3) also has a "pending" — different field, different meaning.

=== PAGINATION (every list endpoint) ===
Rows      -> data.data      (array)
Page info -> data.meta      (current_page, last_page, per_page, total)
Page URLs -> data.links     (first, last, prev, next — null at the edges)
Next page -> add ?page=2

=== HEADS UP: RATE LIMIT ===
/register/donor, /register/charity and /login accept only 5 requests per minute per IP. Going over returns 429 "Too many requests". If registration suddenly stops working while testing, that is why — wait a minute and continue. Nothing is broken.

request.description:
Creates a donor account. Usable immediately — no admin approval needed.

FIELDS
- name         : max 120 chars
- type         : "individual" | "restaurant" | "hotel" | "company"   <- dropdown in the UI
- email        : must not exist as a donor OR a charity
- phone        : max 20 chars
- password     : min 8 chars
- password_confirmation : must match password

RETURNS a token — save it and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every protected request.

Note: re-running this returns 422 (email taken). Change the `donor_email` variable to register again.

response.name: 201 Created
422 Email already taken

request.description:
Creates a charity account. It always starts as status = "pending".

SEND AS multipart/form-data, not JSON — `license_document` is an uploaded file.
If you are not attaching a file you may send plain JSON instead; both work.

IMPORTANT FOR THE APP FLOW
A pending charity CAN log in and call /me — so it can see its own status — but it CANNOT use any charity feature until an admin approves it. Show a "waiting for approval" screen while status is "pending".

FIELDS
- name             : max 120 chars
- email            : must not exist as a donor OR a charity
- phone            : max 20 chars
- password         : min 8 chars
- password_confirmation : must match password
- has_kitchen      : true | false  <- true means it can cook raw food. A charity with false is NEVER shown food that needs cooking.
- address          : max 255 chars
- work_start       : "HH:MM" 24h, e.g. "08:00"
- work_end         : "HH:MM" 24h, must be after work_start
- license_document : optional FILE — pdf, jpg, jpeg or png, max 5 MB

HEADS UP: this endpoint echoes back what you sent, so `work_start` comes back as "08:00" and `rating_avg` / `ratings_count` are absent. /login and /me return the stored form ("08:00:00") with those two fields present. Parse the charity defensively, or just re-read it from /me after registering.

request.description:
ONE login endpoint for both account types — do not ask the user whether they are a donor or a charity, the API works it out.

HOW TO ROUTE AFTER LOGIN
1. Read `data.type`:
   "donor"   -> open the donor home screen
   "charity" -> go to step 2
2. For a charity, read `data.user.status`:
   "active"    -> charity home screen
   "pending"   -> "waiting for admin approval" screen
   "suspended" -> "account suspended" screen

A pending or suspended charity logs in successfully (200) on purpose, so it can see where it stands.

BODY: email, password. Wrong email or wrong password both return the same 401 "Invalid credentials" — deliberate, so nobody can discover which emails exist.

request.description:
The list that fills the food-category dropdown on the "create donation request" screen. Short and fixed, so it is NOT paginated — `data` is a plain array.

Each item has both `name_ar` and `name_en`; show `name_ar` in the Arabic UI.

`default_needs_cooking` is a suggestion, not a rule: when the donor picks a category, pre-fill the "needs cooking?" switch from this value but let them change it. It matters because food that needs cooking is never shown to a charity without a kitchen.

response.name: 200 OK

item.name: Notifications (donor & charity)
item.description:
The signed-in account's own feed. The SAME two endpoints serve donors and charities — the API works out who you are from the token, and you only ever see your own notifications.

WHEN A NOTIFICATION APPEARS
- request_accepted   -> to the DONOR, the moment a charity accepts. payload: charity_name, eta_minutes.
- handover_confirmed -> to the CHARITY, once the donor confirms the food changed hands. payload: donor_name, charity_name, donor_id, charity_id.

The admin has its own separate feed under Admin > Notifications.

Poll GET /notifications?is_read=false for the unread badge.

request.description:
Paginated 15 per page, newest first.

FILTERS (both optional)
- is_read : "true" | "false" | "1" | "0"
- type    : "request_accepted" | "handover_confirmed"

Rows -> data.data · page info -> data.meta · page links -> data.links

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Marks one of YOUR notifications read.

Returns 404 if the id belongs to someone else — donors and charities are numbered separately, so an id alone is never enough to identify a row.

response.name: 404 Belongs to another account

item.name: Donor — Donations
item.description:
Everything the donor does with a donation request.

THE LIFECYCLE (read this once, it explains every screen)

  pending  ──charity accepts──>  accepted  ──donor confirms──>  picked_up
     │                              │                               │
     │                              │                               └──charity files numbers──> completed
     ├──donor cancels──> cancelled  │
     └──expiry passes──> expired    └──donor cancels──> cancelled

The donor screens map to it like this:
  pending    -> "waiting for a charity to accept" (poll GET /donor/requests/{id})
  accepted   -> show the charity card + eta_minutes, and the "Delivered" button
  picked_up  -> handover done; show the rating prompt
  completed  -> the charity filed its distribution numbers
  cancelled  -> show cancel_reason
  expired    -> nobody took it in time

body.raw:
{
  "food_category_id": 1,
  "quantity_desc": "about 20 meals",
  "description": "rice and chicken",
  "valid_until": "2026-08-30 20:00:00",
  "pickup_until": "2026-08-30 18:00:00",
  "pickup_address": "Aleppo - Al-Furqan, near the mosque",
  "contact_phone": "0999999999"
}

request.description:
Publishes a new donation request. It starts as status "pending" and becomes visible to every eligible charity.

FIELDS
- food_category_id : REQUIRED. An id from GET /food-categories.
- quantity_desc    : REQUIRED. Free text, max 150. The donor's rough estimate ("about 20 meals", "3 trays"). Real numbers come from the charity later.
- description      : optional, max 255. Ingredients, allergy notes, anything extra.
- needs_cooking    : OPTIONAL true/false. If you omit it, the API fills it from the category's default_needs_cooking. Send it only when the donor overrides the switch.
- valid_until      : REQUIRED. "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS". Must be in the FUTURE. Last moment the food is still edible.
- pickup_until     : REQUIRED. Same format. Must be in the future AND not later than valid_until. Last moment the donor can hand it over.
- pickup_address   : REQUIRED, max 255. Written location — the donor always types where they are.
- latitude         : OPTIONAL, -90..90. Map pin.
- longitude        : OPTIONAL, -180..180. Map pin.
- contact_phone    : REQUIRED, max 20.

ABOUT THE MAP PIN: latitude and longitude are optional, but they travel together — sending one without the other is a 422. Send both, or neither.

WHY needs_cooking MATTERS: food flagged as needing cooking is NEVER shown to a charity that has no kitchen. Pre-tick the switch from the category's default_needs_cooking and let the donor change it.

ONE AT A TIME
A donor may only have one request in `pending` or `accepted`. Trying to create a second returns 422 with `errors.active_request_id` — the message carries the id of the request already in flight, so the app can jump straight to it.
Once the donor confirms the handover the request no longer blocks a new one, even though the charity has yet to file its distribution numbers.

request.description:
Full details of one of the donor's own requests. This is the endpoint the "waiting" and "accepted" screens poll.

WHAT APPEARS WHEN
- charity      : null while pending. Once a charity accepts, it holds that charity's card: id, name, phone, address, logo_url, rating_avg, ratings_count, completed_donations_count.
- eta_minutes  : null while pending. After acceptance, the minutes the charity said it needs to arrive — show it as "arriving in about N minutes".
- rating_avg   : null when the charity has no ratings yet. Show "no ratings yet", not a zero.
- distribution : null until the charity files its numbers (families_count, individuals_count, area).
- rating       : null until the donor rates. Non-null means already rated — hide the rating button.

Requesting another donor's request id returns 404 (not 403) on purpose, so ids cannot be probed.

request.description:
Cancels the request.

ALLOWED ONLY from status "pending" or "accepted". Anything else (already picked_up, completed, cancelled) returns 422 — so hide the cancel button once the status leaves those two.

BODY
- reason : optional, max 255. Comes back as cancel_reason on the request.

response.name: 200 OK
422 Cannot cancel from this state

request.description:
The donor states the food has changed hands. This is what moves the request to "picked_up".

HOW IT WORKS ON SCREEN
1. The charity arrives and collects the food.
2. The donor taps "Delivered" on the request screen.
3. Send this request — no body is needed.
4. On success the status becomes "picked_up" — now show the rating prompt.

BODY
- None. Send an empty request.

WHAT HAPPENS BEHIND THE SCENES
The backend records a notification for the admin ("charity X received from donor Y") and one for the charity. You do not need to do anything for that.

ERRORS
- 422 if the request is not in status "accepted" (already confirmed, cancelled, or never accepted). Do not retry on 422.
- 404 if the request does not belong to this donor.

response.name: 200 OK
422 Not in accepted state

request.description:
The donor rates the charity for this donation.

WHEN IT IS ALLOWED: from status "picked_up" onwards (picked_up or completed). The donor does not have to wait for the charity to file its distribution numbers.

ONE RATING PER DONATION. A second attempt returns 422. Before showing the rating button, check the `rating` field on the request — if it is not null, it was already rated.

BODY
- stars   : REQUIRED, integer 1..5
- comment : optional, max 500

The charity's rating_avg and ratings_count are recalculated immediately.

response.name: 201 Created
422 Already rated

item.name: Charity — Donations
item.description:
What an APPROVED charity can do.

GATE: every request in this folder requires the charity's status to be "active". A pending or suspended charity gets 403 "Charity account is not active". Log in, read data.user.status, and show the waiting/suspended screen instead of these features.

THE KITCHEN RULE (the most important rule in the project): a charity with has_kitchen = false NEVER sees food flagged needs_cooking = true. It is filtered out of the available list, and even a hand-crafted accept call for such a request is rejected with 422.

request.description:
Open requests this charity is eligible to take, newest first, 15 per page.

A request appears here only if ALL of these hold:
1. status is "pending" (nobody has taken it)
2. valid_until is still in the future
3. if it needs cooking, this charity has a kitchen
4. this charity did not previously no-show on it

Same pagination shape as the donor list: rows in data.data, page info in data.meta.

Each row includes pickup_until so the charity can judge whether it can get there within its own working hours — that judgement is left to the charity, the API does not filter on it.

response.name: 200 OK
403 Charity not approved yet

request.description:
The charity claims the request. Status becomes "accepted" and the donor is now waiting for this charity.

BODY
- eta_minutes : REQUIRED, integer 5..480. How long the charity needs to reach the donor. The donor sees it as "arriving in about N minutes".

FIRST COME, FIRST SERVED
One request goes to exactly one charity. If another charity claimed it a moment earlier you get 422 "Request is no longer available" — refresh the available list.

KITCHEN RULE
A charity with has_kitchen = false cannot accept food where needs_cooking = true. Those requests never appear in the available list, and a direct attempt returns 422.

WHAT THE DONOR SEES
The backend notifies the donor which charity accepted and the ETA. Nothing extra to send.

response.name: 200 OK
422 Already taken

request.description:
Everything this charity has taken — its work queue and its history. Newest first, 15 per page, same pagination shape as the other lists.

Group them in the UI by status: accepted = still to collect, picked_up = collected, awaiting distribution numbers, completed = done.

request.description:
The admin's activity feed. Right now it is the handover trail: which charity received from which donor.

NOTIFICATION TYPES
- "handover_confirmed" -> the donor confirmed the food changed hands. payload carries donor_id, donor_name, charity_id, charity_name.
- "request_accepted"   -> a charity claimed a request. This one is addressed to the donor, so it does NOT appear in this admin feed.

FILTERS (both optional)
- is_read : true | false
- type    : one of the types above

Paginated 15 per page, newest first. Rows are in data.data.

NOTE: this endpoint returns ONLY notifications addressed to the admin. Donor and charity notifications are not visible here.

response.name: 200 OK
